scope: A disposable Kubernetes v1.36.1 Kind cluster reconciles native Prometheus Operator Prometheus, ServiceMonitor, and PodMonitor resources. Namespace-scoped discovery RBAC and selector labels limit scraping to two safe synthetic CPU workloads. Prometheus API queries prove no samples before monitor enrollment and exact per-workload stage, measured latency, and quality markers after enrollment. A supplementary check runs the checksum-pinned llama.cpp b9519 CPU server with a tiny pinned model, enables its native Prometheus exporter, and compares a fixed four-token completion with the observed increase in its generation-token counter. The case then observes target retirement and the absence of synthetic series under a 30-second lookback after each monitor removal. The native llama.cpp target remains healthy. GPU/DCGM telemetry, native training signals, production attribution, default query lookback, and durable retention have separate evidence requirements.

checks.claim: Before monitor enrollment healthy fixture workloads have no scrape targets or samples
The native monitors expose exact training progress, measured timings, and labeled model quality
ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor produce separate scrapes and leave the healthy unselected fixture out
The scraping identity is scoped to discovery in the fixture namespace
Prometheus observes the bounded native llama.cpp generation counter increase
Removing the training monitor retires its target and 30s-lookback series while inference and native llama remain available
Removing the inference monitor retires its target and 30s-lookback series while native llama remains available
The real PyTorch workload exposes a zero optimizer-step baseline before training
Prometheus scrapes step count and measured loss from a real pinned PyTorch CPU training run
